title: Infantry Weapons Officer (III) (CWO5 to CWO2) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
3.     MOS 0306, Infantry Weapons Officer (III) (CWO5 to CWO2) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. The Marine gunner is a CWO specifically trained in the
employment and training of infantry battalion organic weapons, gear and
assigned personnel and in the basics of combat marksmanship as defined by the
current version of reference (cg). Gunners are special staff officers
employed as the principal advisor to commanders at all levels. They assist
in the development of training and employment plans designed to ensure
mission essential task (MET) compliance. They help design and vet the
weaponeering and training policies of the commander and help to disseminate
information to the units personnel regarding such policies. They generate
and quantify reports on the units technical and tactical weaponeering
proficiency and brief the unit commander as to where each subordinate unit
sits in regard to his intent. They mentor the officers and Marines of the
unit in all applicable mechanical, doctrinal and conceptual weaponeering and
training matters, as required, to improve the general effectiveness and
proficiency of the command. They have oversight of the unit's ammunition
allocation and annual weapons requalification and certification programs.
They accommodate all weapons organic to the MAGTF in accordance with the
current version of reference (cf). Additional duties will include Marine
Expeditionary Unit (MEU) gunner, battalion landing team (BLT) gunner in
support of a MEU, team new equipment training (NET), new weapons systems and
gear research and development, foreign weapons.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have a minimum GT score of 110.

        (2) Must be a gunnery sergeant with a minimum of one year time in
grade (TIG) at the time of application.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.


                                            1-20                    Enclosure (1)
 1106                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (4) Must be gunnery sergeant who has previously served in an
infantry, reconnaissance, light armored reconnaissance or Marine Special
Operations Battalion in the 0321, 0363, 0369, or 0372 MOSs.

        (5) Or must have previously served in an infantry, light armored
reconnaissance, or reconnaissance battalion as a gunnery sergeant in the
0321, 0363, 0369, or 0372 MOSs.

            (6) Must have attended one or more of the following:

                (a) Reconnaissance Team Leader Course (M10NAN2).

                (b) Advanced Mortar Course (M10H5H2 or M03H5H4).

                (c) Infantry Unit Leaders Course (M10H5K2 or M03H5K4).

                (d) Advanced Anti-Armor Course (M10MUR2 or M03MUR4).

                (e) Advanced Machinegun Course (M10H6A2 or M03H6A4).

                (f) Light Armored Reconnaissance Leader Course (M10H3W2).

                (g) Advanced Assault Marine Course (M10MUS2 or M03MUS4).

                (h) Advanced Infantry Marine Course (M10M3X2 or M03M3X4).

                (i) Infantry Small Unit Leaders Course (M100302 or M030304).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Infantry Weapons Officer Course (IWOC) (M02H3Z4),
Quantico, VA.

        (2) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (e), Infantry Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Tactical Ground Range Control Officer.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
